record.paper_title: On free curves and related open problems
record.context_brief: ν from degree and analytic singularity types
record.original_question: Let C:f=0 be a reduced plane curve in P^2 with isolated singularities, and let ν(C)=max_j dim N(f)_j be its freeness-defect invariant. Is ν(C) determined by just two pieces of data: the degree of C and the list of analytic isomorphism types of its isolated singularities?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.8. Let C : f = 0 be a reduced plane curve P2. Then the invariant ν(C) is determined by the degree of C and the list of the analytic types of the isolated singularities of C.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture in recent work on free plane curves (late 2023). Subsequent works from 2024–2025 on the defect of plane curves discuss and provide partial evidence (e.g., for irreducible curves with simple singularities and certain line/curve arrangements), and a related conjecture about combinatorial determination of $\nu$ for line arrangements is also explicitly listed as open. No proof or counterexample to the general statement was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Defect of irreducible plane curves with simple singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the defect ν(C) for irreducible plane curves with ADE singularities; treats the conjecture in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses the conjecture only in restricted classes, indicating it remains generally open.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on plane curves related to freeness
status_evidence.snippet: Further remarks on ν(C) and freeness-related invariants of plane curves (2025).
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent 2025 paper continues to investigate ν(C) without resolving the general determination question.

status_evidence.title: On free curves and related open problems
